rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desires for wealth, children, and longevity make the vulnerable susceptible to polytheistic superstition at altars, graves, and mausoleums.
rows.anchor: wealth and children, life and wealth and other similar wants have always remained a factor that has led people to polytheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab idolaters did not regard their deities as creators, but especially angels as influential in sustenance, wealth, and children.
rows.anchor: They did not regard their deities to be the creators of the heavens and the earth but in matters like sustenance, wealth and children

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They worshipped jinn for power over sickness, health, and longevity, even sacrificing children to appease them; this verse refutes such superstition.
rows.anchor: They contended that if they did not sacrifice a boy or a girl to keep them happy, they will kill all their children.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that God created humans from clay, then from a sperm drop, and made them pairs introduces the following argument.
rows.anchor: form an introduction for what is stated next.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God created and developed every part of this world, the idolaters cannot deny His creative power.
rows.anchor: every part of this house was made and developed by God and this is a reality which they cannot deny

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator who established human generations and created people in pairs is fully able to provide for their sustenance, offspring, and lifespan; there is no reason to delegate these affairs to other deities.
rows.anchor: what was the difficulty that afflicted Him that He was compelled to consign matters like sustenance, offspring and longevity to others?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows when a woman becomes pregnant, whether her child is male or female, when she gives birth, and the child's form and nature.
rows.anchor: He who has set the family of Adam in procession knows when a woman will get pregnant and whether she carries a male or a female offspring

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs accepted God as Creator but doubted that He knew every affair across the vast universe, which led them to assign affairs to partners.
rows.anchor: they had this doubt that how can He be aware of all the affairs of this huge and expansive universe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters doubted God's awareness of the vast universe and assigned sustenance, children, and lifespans to partners.
rows.anchor: consigned many matters like sustenance, children and life-span to His partners and associates

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asserting that even the smallest event is within the Creator's knowledge, the Qur'an answers the Arabs' doubt about God's awareness of all details.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has struck on this notion of theirs and asserted that the smallest of events

rows.speaker: Zamakhsharī
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī reads muʿammar as every person granted a lifespan, long or short, rather than only an old person; Islahi says this is correct.
rows.anchor: Zamakhsharī180 has interpreted this word thus and I think that this is the correct interpretation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person's allotted lifespan, whether short or long, is within God's knowledge and command.
rows.anchor: The age of a person whether short or long is in God’s knowledge and at His bidding.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying a lifespan is written in a register restates God's knowledge and strengthens the assurance that nothing will be forgotten.
rows.anchor: This style further strengthens what was said above.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that this is easy for God answers doubts about His knowing minute details: no task requires a helper because nothing is difficult for Him.
rows.anchor: no task is difficult for God so that He may require some helper to accomplish it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verses refute polytheism from another angle, through the harmonious ordering of nature.
rows.anchor: These verses, through another aspect, refute polytheism and deities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opposing elements in nature can lead people toward polytheism, a tendency the Qur'an counters in several ways.
rows.anchor: conflict between opposing elements of nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent opposites in nature also show deep harmony, indicating that one supreme power governs them for the universe's collective benefit.
rows.anchor: besides their outward opposing nature there is deep harmony between them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the sweet and bitter seas meet, neither changes the other's character; a supreme being keeps each within its bounds, as also stated in 55:19-20.
rows.anchor: Both thump into each other but this never happens that the bitter one is able to turn the sweet one bitter or vice versa.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both seas provide fresh meat and pearls, and their waters serve ships that carry people to seek God's bounty and give thanks.
rows.anchor: they are able to obtain fresh meat in their long sea-journeys

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should look beyond apparent contradiction to the harmony through which the one powerful, living God puts nature's opposing forces at human service and prompts gratitude.
rows.anchor: they should also reflect on the harmony found between them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day and night appear opposed but complement each other, and both are necessary for the world and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: Both in their apparent outlook seem to be opposite to one another yet there exists great harmony between them as if they complement one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are not deities: their existence shows they are serving creation, and their fixed courses serve human needs.
rows.anchor: both with their fixed timetables fervently serve the needs of man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is Lord and owns sovereignty summarizes the preceding signs of His majesty, power, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: this God Whose majesty, power and wisdom people observe is their Lord and to Him belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitmir means the thin covering over a date seed.
rows.anchor: The word ٍریِمْطِق refers to the thin covering over the seed of a date.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God have no role whatsoever in the creation and management of the world.
rows.anchor: those whom they invoke and worship besides God have no role whatsoever in the creation and management of the affairs of this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istajāba lahu means that someone responded to a person or listened to that person's invocation.
rows.anchor: The expression ابَجَتْاس لَه means

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities' helplessness is plain in this world and will be clearer in the Hereafter: they will not hear invocations in distress, and even if they hear, cannot answer.
rows.anchor: The verse points out the helplessness and baselessness of their deities:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities the idolaters invented never existed, so they could neither hear worshippers nor answer their prayers.
rows.anchor: The deities which the Idolaters worshipped

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If worshipped beings actually existed, the righteous among them, such as angels and prophets, will openly disown their worshippers.
rows.anchor: the righteous among them like the angels and the prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil beings such as jinn and devils will tell their worshippers that their choice was their misfortune and that they cannot help them.
rows.anchor: The evil among those worshipped like the jinn and the devils

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities were unaware of being invoked for help in this life and could not answer the idolaters.
rows.anchor: these deities were unaware that in this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Judgment, the deities will reject that they were worshipped as associates with God, confirming their inability to answer their worshippers.
rows.anchor: on the Day of Judgement they will reject they were worshipped as associated deities to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi connects the denial of worship to 34:40-41, where angels deny being worshipped and say that people actually worshipped the jinn.
rows.anchor: The details of this rejection have been cited in Sūrah Sabā’ thus:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite khabīr is left without a definite article to convey the magnitude of the one truly cognizant.
rows.anchor: The word ریِبَخ is not defined by an definite particle to portray its magnitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a real knower can disclose hidden matters that will later appear; people should heed this admonition rather than remain captive to fancies.
rows.anchor: only a real cognizant being knows what is hidden from the eyes of people and which will one day manifest before them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 15-17 intensify the preceding admonition and address everyone; the Messenger's tireless efforts to awaken people do not mean God needs their response.
rows.anchor: so that everyone should fully listen up that all this elaborate arrangement made for their education and reminding

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly self-sufficient and praiseworthy in His attributes, while people need Him in this world and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: and praiseworthy in His attributes; it is these people who need God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can destroy all people and bring a new creation in their place if He wills; doing so is no difficulty for Him.
rows.anchor: if He wants He can destroy all of them and bring forth a new creation in their place.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God mercifully grants respite despite people's ingratitude and continues to give them time.
rows.anchor: It is His mercy and favour on them that in spite of their ungrateful attitude He is continuing to give

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is perfect and complete, with no dependence on anything outside Himself; His relationship with creation rests on mercy and favor, not need.
rows.anchor: God’s being is perfect and complete and this perfection of His is not dependent on anything external to His being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says God created people to show generosity and mercy, not to gain any benefit for Himself.
rows.anchor: I did not create [people] to receive benefit for Myself; in fact, I created them to show them mercy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Judgment, each soul bears its own burden and no soul can carry another's.
rows.anchor: on that day no soul will bear the burden of another; on the contrary, each soul shall bear its own burden.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun qualified by muṯqalah is omitted; the full phrase would be nafsun muṯqalatun, a soul burdened by its sins.
rows.anchor: The noun qualified by the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governing noun before ḥaml is omitted, as is kāna's noun al-madʿū; Islahi says these omissions are common in classical Arabic.
rows.anchor: the mud@āf (governing noun) is suppressed before ْلِمَح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul burdened by sins will find no one to share its load, not even its closest relative.
rows.anchor: it will find none to help it even if it invokes help from its closest relative.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The virtuous did not share the sinner's wrongdoing in the world, so they will not become companions in sin in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: if they did not accompany its sins in the previous world, why will they become its companions in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers are themselves engulfed by their sins and therefore cannot help anyone else.
rows.anchor: they themselves will be buried in their sins

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should use the respite God gives, since their disobedience cannot harm Him or His Messenger and only brings their own ruin.
rows.anchor: they should remember that neither will they be able to harm God in any way nor His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assures the Prophet to warn people, but the warning benefits only those who use their faculties, fear their unseen Lord, and persevere in prayer; he should leave the others to God.
rows.anchor: his warning can only be effective on those who use their intellect and other faculties of cognizance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is mentioned because it is the foremost outward expression of faith and a sign of fearing God while unseen.
rows.anchor: adhering to the prayer is the foremost manifestation of faith and a symbol of God’s fear.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone heedless of prayer is heedless of God, however strongly that person verbally claims faith.
rows.anchor: He who is heedless of the prayer is heedless of God even though he may make tall claims to faith by his tongue.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek to shed sin and purify themselves should be diligent in prayer instead of relying on false support.
rows.anchor: should be diligent and vigilant in the prayer instead of relying on false support.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification benefits the person who acquires it; God needs no worship or obedience, His servants need Him, and all return to Him.
rows.anchor: it is His servants who are in need, and everyone is set to return to Him alone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III (verses 19-28) moves to the kinds of people who accept faith and those deprived of it, using contrasts in nature to illuminate this difference.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses state the types of people who will accept faith and the types who will be deprived from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light and darkness, heat and cold, and fertile land flourishing in rain versus barren land despite abundant rain illustrate different human tendencies.
rows.anchor: there are fertile lands which become lush green because of rain and there also barren lands which in spite of abundant rain do not bear any produce.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is like rain: vibrant, living hearts benefit from it, while those dead in heart and mind are deprived of its blessing.
rows.anchor: which is pouring down on them in the form of the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created natural opposites for the universe's benefit and gives respite to people inclined to vice as well as those inclined to virtue.
rows.anchor: for the overall benefit of the universe in a similar manner He has given respite to people who like vice
